Subject: GST treatment for prepaid credits — Oxbridge subsidiaries

Hi Neha,

Quick question from procurement as we prepare a prepaid credit purchase across a few Oxbridge entities. We plan to buy USD-denominated prepaid credits from Redwood and allocate them to multiple subsidiaries (India, Singapore, UK, and two EU entities). Two specific asks: 

1) For the India entity, is GST charged at invoice time or do we apply reverse-charge when our Indian entity consumes the credits? (Procurement prefers not to have GST on the invoice if reverse-charge is possible.)

2) For the EU entities, can you validate VAT IDs in bulk (we have 6 VAT numbers across two subsidiaries) and confirm whether B2B reverse-charge applies or Redwood needs to charge VAT at point of sale?

We can share the list of VAT/GST numbers but would like to understand Redwood's preferred workflow (self-billing, invoice-level reverse-charge notation, or require local tax registration). Also any template you prefer for bulk validation would help.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if easier.

Priyanka
Procurement Manager
Oxbridge Labs

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GST treatment for prepaid credits — Oxbridge subsidiaries

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the clear note. Quick answers and a suggested next step below.

Summary answers:
- India: GST treatment depends on whether the place of supply is India (services consumed in India) and whether the buyer (your India legal entity) is registered for GST. If your India entity is the buyer and is GST-registered, reverse-charge can apply in many cases when the supply is classified as an import of services, but we need your GSTIN and a short description of how credits are used to confirm.
- EU: For B2B sales to EU-registered businesses, reverse-charge usually applies if we have validated a VAT ID that matches the purchasing legal entity and the place of supply is the buyer's member state. We'll validate the VAT IDs and return a validation result for each number.

What I need from you to proceed: a single CSV using our template (attached) with columns: legal_entity_name, billing_entity, country, VAT/GST number, invoice_bill_to_email, planned_monthly_consumption_USD. Please include the India GSTIN for the India entity.

Attached: vatid-upload-template.csv (simple one-line example included). Once you upload, we will run automated checks (VIES for EU, GSTIN check for India) and flag any numbers that need manual evidence (certificate or business registration doc).

Options for invoice handling (high level):
- Self-billing / invoice annotation: We can issue invoices with a reverse-charge note where applicable (recommended for EU B2B when VAT IDs validate).
- Reducing upfront tax friction: For prepaids where the buyer is a non-Indian entity consuming services outside India, we can invoice net of GST, but we must document place-of-supply.
- If manual validation is required for any numbers, that will delay issuance of final invoice tax treatment by 2–3 business days.

Next steps:
1) Please return the populated CSV to me (neha_kapoor@redwood.com).
2) Ben will follow up on commercial terms for prepaid commit and any billing cadence adjustments.
3) We will prepare a short amendment to the MSA for prepaid credits (DocuSign draft) if you need specific wording around tax liability.

If useful, we can book a 20-minute call this afternoon — otherwise send the CSV and we'll start validation.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Revenue Ops — Billing & Tax
Redwood Inference

Hi Priyanka — quick note from the commercial side.

Thanks for raising this. To reduce billing friction while Neha's team validates VAT/GST, we can do either:

1) Issue a provisional invoice (amount only) for the prepaid credits and then issue a final tax-bearing invoice once validations are complete, or
2) Move to a split billing approach (UK/EU billed to UK entity, India billed to India entity) if that maps cleanly to your finance setup.

We're also open to offering deferred payment terms for the India-framed portion pending GST resolution (short 14-day deferred window) — happy to include this in the amendment if helpful. If you can confirm which path you prefer we will include it in the DocuSign draft Neha mentioned.

I attached a short collection schedule proposal for visibility.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Priyanka — thanks, received the CSV you sent this morning and we ran our checks. Short summary below and immediate asks.

Validation results (automated first pass):
- 4 numbers validated successfully via VIES/GST portal (EU1, EU2, SG, UK).
- 2 numbers flagged for manual evidence (India GSTIN format OK but business name mismatch; second EU VAT number returned "inactive").

What Redwood needs to proceed to final invoicing: 
- For the India GSTIN flagged: please upload a scanned copy of the GST registration certificate (signed page or GST portal screenshot) and confirm the India legal entity that will be billed.
- For the EU VAT that came back inactive: please confirm whether that VAT belongs to an alternate legal entity (we can re-run validation) or provide your VAT registration certificate.

Planned handling:
- For the 4 validated entities we'll issue tax-annotated invoices reflecting reverse-charge where applicable.
- For the 2 pending, we'll either (a) provisionally invoice net of VAT with a follow-up tax-bearing invoice once evidence is provided, or (b) apply tax on the invoice and credit/re-issue if evidence supports reverse-charge — whichever you prefer (Ben, see collection/provisional options below).

Timeline: once we receive the two supporting docs we expect to finalize tax treatment and reissue any impacted invoices within 2 business days.

DocuSign: I have uploaded a draft prepaid amendment with the deferred payment language Ben suggested — link below. If Oxbridge is OK with provisional invoicing for the two pending numbers, we can close the amendment and proceed.
